title: Boundary-Driven Anisotropic Coarsening in Conserved Phase Separation
summary: Universal scaling in phase separation is typically assumed to be isotropic in systems with conserved dynamics. Here we show that boundary forcing alone can break this dynamical scaling symmetry, leading to anisotropic coarsening, with different effective global growth laws observed parallel and perpendicular to the boundary. We consider a ternary mixture with two conserved components and a passive species undergoing surface evaporation, which provides a simple setting to investigate this effect.
